candidates.reason: For the issue of breach of contract and the standard of care in delivery delay, cases such as Nettleship v Weston establish the objective standard of care. Robinson v Chief Constable supports breach finding where duty and foreseeability are established. The initial hybrid shortlist cases (Bolton v Stone, Paris v Stepney Borough Council etc.) also consider standards of care but did not appear with top scores in search. Davis Contractors clarifies non-frustration despite delays, relevant to contractual performance.

recoverability of lost profits damages contract remoteness
candidates.reason: Hadley v Baxendale and Victoria Laundry are classic authorities on remoteness of contract damages involving lost profits, distinguishing ordinary and exceptional losses. Spartan Steel explains recoverability of loss consequential on physical damage versus pure economic loss. Adams v Lindsell concerns contract formation. Dunlop Pneumatic Tyre and Caparo consider damages and foreseeability broadly related to loss but with emphasis on contractual context.
